te: Pre-meeting video · Transport and logistics links to deep-sea ports on the Andaman coast
Phuket and Ranong ports, and the Smart Port
se: The meeting studied policies and plans to develop commercial deep-sea ports on the Andaman coast, safety at sea, and the use of digital technology towards a Smart Port, with the Marine Department, the Port Authority of Thailand, the Customs Department and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society. The Marine Department explained plans to improve the channel of Phuket deep-sea port for large ships and cruise ships, while Ranong port is still limited by channel depth, space behind the wharf and transport links. The Port Authority of Thailand explained phase 3 of Ranong port, now under environmental impact assessment (EIA), and its truck queue system. The Customs Department explained work on customs procedures and data links, and the limits on tracking goods after they leave customs control. The Ministry of Digital Economy and Society described telecommunications networks in the South. The subcommittee proposed studying the value for money of Andaman ports, making the truck queue system efficient and fair, and linking data through the National Single Window (NSW). The meeting asked the agencies to send further explanations in writing. The agenda also included a report on a study visit to Laem Chabang port in Chon Buri province, which the meeting summary does not describe.
it: Policies and plans to develop commercial deep-sea ports on the Andaman coast, safety at sea, and digital technology towards a Smart Port
Plans for Phuket deep-sea port, and the limits of Ranong port
Phase 3 of Ranong port (under environmental impact assessment) and the truck queue system
Customs procedures, data links, and telecommunications networks in the South
Agencies to send further explanations and information in writing, for policy recommendations

te: The Pak Bara deep-sea port, linking the two coasts, and the Thai Canal idea
se: The meeting studied the feasibility and effects of the Pak Bara deep-sea port project in Satun province, and ways to link logistics between the Gulf of Thailand and the Andaman coast. It heard a logistics expert, an adviser to the subcommittee and representatives of a private group that studies the Thai Canal idea. They said a port on the Andaman coast should mainly be an international trade gateway (Gateway Port) for Thai goods, rather than a transshipment port, and that a master plan for the South should come before choosing a site, looking at the potential of existing ports, especially Ranong port. On the Thai Canal idea, route 9A linking Krabi–Trang with Nakhon Si Thammarat–Songkhla, about 135 kilometres long, the meeting raised concerns about the large investment, value for money, sea levels and salt water intrusion. The meeting took note and will use the observations in its study report, focusing on making the most of existing ports and infrastructure.
it: Feasibility and effects of the Pak Bara deep-sea port project in Satun province, and logistics links between the Gulf of Thailand and the Andaman coast
The role of an Andaman port: international trade gateway (Gateway Port) or transshipment port
A master plan for the South, and the potential of existing ports, especially Ranong port
The Thai Canal idea, route 9A, linking the Gulf of Thailand and the Andaman coast
5 observations, such as studying cargo demand and value for money before fixing a port site, and involving the public from the start of a project
